newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end higher led by banks, tea shares.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end higher led by banks, tea shares.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed higher on Tuesday on retail buying of banking and plantation shares triggered by belief that they would report good corporate earnings, brokers said.
The all share index closed 2.48 points higher at 595.52 as gainers led decliners by 31 to 15.
"Retail investors had a lot to do with price rises among banking and tea shares," said Hussain Gani of brokerage John Keells.
He said they believed banks and plantation firms would post improved corporate results in the quarter to September 30.
Commercial Bank rose 9.25 rupees to 120, Hatton National Bank six to 206, Merchant Bank two to 21 rupees and Tea Smallholder 50 cents to 22.75 rupees.
Turnover was a moderately active 51.92 million rupees.
Brokers said many local and foreign institutional buyers were collecting Sampath Bank shares, which they thought offered good value at current prices.
"Sellers of Sampath have been around for some time. Now there are many buyers too," said a trader at brokerage CT Smith.
